# Logistics 0.2.1-alpha.5

- Mobile File Browser adds a tile view with offline thumbnails, keeps your place when returning to a folder, and improves filename search and hardware shortcuts. You can move selections across supported destinations and manage local archives from File Browser.
- New and Change Template show the notebook pattern and the selected Paper Pro or Paper Pro Move proportions. Move forms fit the available page area while retaining existing ink. Changing a template preserves handwriting.
- The video timeline shows chapter starts and provides Previous and Next chapter actions on desktop and mobile. Supported renderers offer subtitle brightness controls. iOS uses a compatibility path for affected local Xvid AVI files. Physical iOS Picture in Picture, Xvid playback, and Apple TV chapter behavior still have device checks pending.
- iOS AirPlay can retry a stalled connection at the last confirmed playback position. If recovery fails, the player shows how to retry or return to the device. The sleep and reconnect scenario still needs verification on a physical Duo and Apple TV.
- The IDE shows source and excluded folders using the same colors as Project Settings. It preserves recoverable drafts when files change outside the editor and improves how search results open.
- Desktop File Browser can exchange existing paths with native file managers. Finder transfers passed local testing. Additional Explorer and Dolphin checks are pending.
- Long transfers can show a completion or actionable failure message after you leave the progress view. Mobile background notifications are opt-in and respect the system permission. Messages omit file names and paths. Android system delivery passed emulator checks. iOS system delivery when the app is in the background still needs a physical device check.
- Large selected downloads can resume from verified checkpoints. Protected sessions restrict clipboard and narration actions at the application boundary.

If playback breaks up or skips, include your device, the app build, and the first affected timestamp.
